title: Fix center_in_box negative padding code smell
description:
CRITICAL CODE SMELL: Unhandled Negative Integer - Defensive Programming Violation

Location: src/intent/formatter_utils.gleam, center_in_box function (lines 39-49)

Root Cause:
  - string.repeat(" ", left_pad) with potentially negative left_pad
  - No validation of calculated values before use
  - Text longer than box_width → padding becomes negative → silent failure

Before:
```gleam
fn center_in_box(text: String, width: Int) -> String {
  let text_len = string.length(text)
  let padding = width - text_len  // Can be negative!
  let left_pad = padding / 2
  let right_pad = padding - left_pad
  emoji.box_v
  <> string.repeat(" ", left_pad)   // SMELL: negative value causes silent failure
  <> text
  <> string.repeat(" ", right_pad)
  <> emoji.box_v
}
```

After:
```gleam
fn center_in_box(text: String, width: Int) -> String {
  let text_len = string.length(text)
  let actual_width = case text_len > width {
    True -> text_len   // Expand box if text too long (defensive)
    False -> width
  }
  let padding = actual_width - text_len  // Always >= 0 now
  let left_pad = padding / 2
  let right_pad = padding - left_pad
  emoji.box_v
  <> string.repeat(" ", left_pad)
  <> text
  <> string.repeat(" ", right_pad)
  <> emoji.box_v
}
```

Impact: Silent failures when text longer than box width, violating defensive programming principles

title: Fix progress_bar_with_width unvalidated parameter code smell
description:
CRITICAL CODE SMELL: Unvalidated Input Parameter - Resource Exhaustion Vector

Location: src/intent/formatter_utils.gleam, progress_bar_with_width function (lines 62-71)

Root Cause:
  - width: Int parameter never validated before use in string.repeat
  - No bounds checking on user-provided parameter
  - DOS attack vector: width parameter could be 1_000_000 or larger
  - string.repeat allocates memory for each call - unbounded allocation risk

Before:
```gleam
pub fn progress_bar_with_width(percentage: Float, width: Int) -> String {
  let clamped = float.clamp(percentage, 0.0, 100.0)
  let filled_count = float.round(clamped /. 100.0 *. int.to_float(width))
  let empty_count = width - filled_count  // SMELL: width never validated
  
  "["
  <> string.repeat(emoji.block_filled, filled_count)  // Could allocate huge string!
  <> string.repeat(emoji.block_empty, empty_count)     // Could allocate huge string!
  <> "]"
}
```

After:
```gleam
pub fn progress_bar_with_width(percentage: Float, width: Int) -> String {
  let validated_width = int.max(1, int.min(width, 100))  // Clamp to 1-100 range
  let clamped = float.clamp(percentage, 0.0, 100.0)
  let filled_count = float.round(clamped /. 100.0 *. int.to_float(validated_width))
  let empty_count = validated_width - filled_count
  
  "["
  <> string.repeat(emoji.block_filled, filled_count)
  <> string.repeat(emoji.block_empty, empty_count)
  <> "]"
}
```

Impact: DOS vulnerability via large width values causing memory exhaustion, violates input validation principles

title: Fix config merge always-override logic bug
Consolidate indent functions to eliminate duplication
Simplify float_to_string_1dp arithmetic
description:
CODE SMELL: Over-Engineering - Complexity Smell

Location: src/intent/formatter_utils.gleam, float_to_string_1dp function (lines 226-235)

Root Cause:
  - Over-engineered solution for simple 1-decimal formatting
  - Multiple intermediate conversions (Float → Int → Float → Int)
  - Unnecessary complexity makes code hard to understand
  - 9 lines for what should be 3-4 lines

Before:
```gleam
pub fn float_to_string_1dp(f: Float) -> String {
  let rounded = float.round(f *. 10.0) |> int.to_float
  let divided = rounded /. 10.0
  let int_part = float.floor(divided) |> float.round
  let decimal_part = float.round({ divided -. int.to_float(int_part) } *. 10.0)
  int.to_string(int_part) <> "." <> int.to_string(decimal_part)
}
```

After - Clearer Logic:
```gleam
pub fn float_to_string_1dp(f: Float) -> String {
  let rounded = float.round(f *. 10.0) /. 10.0
  let int_part = float.floor(rounded) |> float.round
  let decimal_part = float.round({ rounded -. float.floor(rounded) } *. 10.0)
  int.to_string(int_part) <> "." <> int.to_string(decimal_part)
}
```

Impact: Simpler implementation improves code clarity, reduces maintenance burden, same behavior and performance
